summary: City leaders put a tax-rate increase to voters, voters say no by a wide margin, and the city rewrites its budget with service cuts.
realLife: Austin voters rejected Proposition Q on Nov. 4, 2025, with more than 63 percent opposed; it would have added about $109 million in property tax revenue. The city manager then released a revised budget that cut social service contracts, EMS, parks, municipal court and public health, and council members warned of fewer paramedics and park upkeep.
sources: KXAN, Austin city manager releases revised budget after voters reject Prop Q, Nov 2025: https://www.kxan.com/news/local/austin/austin-city-manager-releases-revised-budget-after-voters-reject-prop-q/amp/
